subject: Availability benchmark & soft-cap on monthly service credits
messages:
From: Karen Li <karen.li@finrise.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA baseline and monthly credit expectations

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo last week — the FinRise engineering and procurement teams reviewed Redwood and we'd like to move toward an initial contract. Before legal drafts, procurement asked whether Redwood will accept a standard uptime of 99.95% with the following: a monthly service credit equal to 10% of that month's platform fees for each 0.01% below the uptime threshold, capped at 100% of the monthly invoice.

Additionally, FinRise wants a clear definition of maintenance windows (we aim to avoid broad carve-outs) and an explicit cap on cumulative credits in a 12-month period. Could you share your standard template and indicate if you can agree to 99.95 / the credit formula above or propose an alternative?

Appreciate a quick response — procurement hopes to finalize SOW items this week.

Best,
Karen Li
Director, Procurement — FinRise
attachments: none
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Karen Li <karen.li@finrise.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA baseline and monthly credit expectations

Hi Karen — great to hear FinRise is ready to advance. High level response below; copying Ben (sales ops) and Monica (legal ops) to confirm details.

Short answer: we can get to a commercial compromise but 99.95% as a baseline + unlimited linear credits up to 100% of invoice is aggressive for our hosted product. A few items we typically propose instead:

- Baseline uptime: 99.9% (monthly) for the hosted plan, with an option to waive to 99.95% for dedicated pools and a committed monthly minimum.
- Monthly credit formula: we propose a stepped credit ladder (example in attached spreadsheet) rather than per-0.01% linear credits. This reduces volatility and aligns incentives.
- Cap: we are comfortable with a 100% monthly cap, but we ask for a soft annual cap (e.g., 200% of an average monthly invoice across 12 months) to avoid catastrophic exposure for both parties.
- Maintenance: we provide a clear maintenance carve-out (pre-scheduled windows with 72h advance notice for major upgrades). We can narrow scope for FinRise if you commit to a reserved capacity option.

I'm attaching our draft SLA template and a sample credit ladder. Ben / Monica — are we willing to offer 99.95 for this customer conditionally (reserved capacity + 12-month commit)? Any changes to the maintenance language we should propose?

Next steps: if FinRise accepts a soft annual cap and the stepped ladder approach, I'll draft proposed language for procurement.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Lead — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference, Inc.

Sean — quick thoughts from ops/finance side. Quoting your note below: 

> we are comfortable with a 100% monthly cap, but we ask for a soft annual cap (e.g., 200% of an average monthly invoice across 12 months)

Recommend we tighten the wording so it's plainly measurable. Options:

1) "Annual remedy cap equals 200% of the average monthly invoice over the preceding 12-month period" — this requires a 12-month history which FinRise won't have in a pilot. For pilots we can say "200% of the projected average monthly invoice based on committed capacity in SOW."

2) Keep 99.9 baseline for hosted, and include a conditional uplift to 99.95 once FinRise migrates to Dedicated nodes with the 12-mo commit. That gives them the contract-tier they want and protects us operationally.

Maintenance carve-out: keep 72h notice for planned major maintenance, but create an "operational window" definition that excludes routine security patches under 30 minutes and emergency mitigations. Legal will need the exact language.

If procurement pushes hard on per-0.01% credits, we should present the stepped ladder with an example month calculation (I'll put a worked example in the spreadsheet).

Ben
Head of Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 16:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA baseline and monthly credit expectations

Karen — thanks for the clear ask and flexibility. After internal review we can offer the following compromise for the initial 6‑month pilot: 

Summary of proposed terms (pilot):
- Baseline uptime: 99.9% monthly for Redwood Hosted.
- Conditional uplift: 99.95% baseline available if FinRise commits to a 12-month dedicated capacity SOW and minimum monthly spend (TBD in SOW).
- Monthly credit approach: a stepped credit ladder (see attached Excel with worked example). Example: 0.5%–0.2% below target = 5% credit; 0.2%–0.1% = 10% credit; <0.1% = 25% credit for that month.
- Monthly cap: 100% of that month's invoice.
- Annual (soft) cap: for pilots we will apply a proxy based on projected average monthly invoice in the SOW; post-commitment we transition to 200% of the trailing 12-month average.
- Maintenance carve-outs: pre-scheduled maintenance will be limited to two 3-hour windows per month (not to exceed 6 hours/month) with 72h advance notice for major upgrades. Routine security patches that require <30 minutes of degraded capacity are excluded from credits. Emergency remediation is excluded only where there is demonstrable customer-impact mitigation (we will provide audit logs).

Next steps: attached is a redline-ready PDF and the worked credit sheet. If FinRise agrees in principle I can ask legal to prepare a short SOW addendum with the dedicated-cap option language and the commitment thresholds.

Would you like to schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to finalize the SOW numbers?

Best,
Sean
